metadata.description: Map of all conflicts between competing truths, philosophies, or implementations

contradictions.description: Repository name vs. actual implementation scope

side_a.evidence: README describes 'a service offering AI Educational Tools' - implies multi-feature service platform
side_a.implications: Users might expect backend API, database, authentication, actual AI functionality

side_b.position: Repository is only a marketing landing page
side_b.evidence: Index.jsx implements only a marketing page with hero section and feature cards - no actual service functionality
side_b.implications: This is promotional content, not a functioning service

contradictions.recommended_action: Clarify in README that this is the landing page FOR the service, not the service itself

contradictions.description: Prettier configuration intent - extreme line width value

side_a.evidence: printWidth: 99999999 - extreme value clearly intentional, not accidental
side_a.implications: Code will never be line-wrapped, potentially optimized for LLM-generated code readability

side_b.position: Should follow standard web dev practices
side_b.evidence: Standard prettier configs use 80-120 character line widths for human readability
side_b.implications: Long lines may be harder for human developers to read

contradictions.proposed_primary_truth: Side A is intentional but unusual
contradictions.recommended_action: Document the rationale in README or normalize to standard value (80-120)

side_a.implications: Container port 8080 exposed to host port 8080

side_b.position: Vite dev server runs on port 8080
side_b.implications: Dev server listens on port 8080 inside container

contradictions.proposed_primary_truth: Both sides aligned - configuration is correct

contradictions.description: Development workflow model ambiguity - dual paths risk conflict

side_a.position: Use GPT Engineer app for development
side_a.evidence: README: 'Changes made via gptengineer.app will be committed to this repo'
side_a.implications: AI-assisted development via web interface, auto-sync to GitHub

side_b.evidence: README: 'If you clone this repo and push changes, you will have them reflected in the GPT Engineer UI'
side_b.implications: Manual development, commit, push to GitHub, sync back to GPT Engineer

contradictions.proposed_primary_truth: Both are true but potentially conflicting
contradictions.recommended_action: Document which workflow is primary; warn against mixing both approaches
contradictions.impact: High risk of merge conflicts if developers use different workflows

contradictions.description: Commit message depth vs. actual change magnitude

side_a.evidence: Commit message: 'Initial commit' - generic, minimal description
side_a.implications: Appears to be a small, simple commit

side_b.evidence: Commit changes: 13 files, 6,055 lines added - entire project structure created
side_b.implications: Major repository initialization, not a trivial commit

contradictions.proposed_primary_truth: Generic message is standard for scaffold generation
contradictions.recommended_action: None required; this is typical LLM/automation behavior
contradictions.impact: Low - commit message doesn't affect functionality
contradictions.notes: Common pattern for automated code generation tools; not a real contradiction, just typical LLM brevity

key_findings: C1 and C4 require immediate documentation updates (critical/high priority)
C2 is a minor anomaly requiring documentation or normalization
C3 is not actually a contradiction - configuration is properly aligned
C5 is a typical LLM artifact pattern, not a real issue
llm_artifact_patterns: Generic commit messages for substantial changes (C5)
Unusual configuration choices without documented rationale (C2)
Ambiguous documentation that doesn't clarify edge cases (C1, C4)
